absent: Locking discipline and concurrency rules for PCI, personality, pidfd and traffic-control state.
Transition triggers and full lifecycle graphs for link and selective IDE stream states beyond the encoded values.
Implementation of ioctl handling, netlink handling and policer enforcement behind the UAPI constants.
Memory ownership, allocation and lifetime rules for the described records.
Error codes and recovery behavior beyond the failure latches and stale-data notes.

findings.text: A PCI integrity capability exposes its feature word at a small fixed offset and its control word a few bytes later. The feature word packs one-bit presence indicators for link operation, selective operation, flow-through operation, partial header protection, aggregation, integrity checksum, key management and config coverage, alongside a multi-bit selector for supported cipher suites with value zero selecting a 256-bit authenticated suite with short tag, a small field counting link traffic classes, a wider field counting selective streams, and a high-bit TEE-limited indicator. The control word carries a single flow-through enable. The first link stream block starts at a fixed low offset with an eight-byte stride.

Each link stream occupies an eight-byte window with control at the window start and status four bytes in. Control combines a stream enable, three two-bit transmit aggregation selectors for distinct packet classes, a checksum enable, a multi-bit partial-encryption mode, a cipher selector drawn from the capability set, a traffic-class selector and a high-byte stream identifier. Status exposes a low-nibble stream state plus a top-bit latch recording arrival of a failure message.

Selective streams expose capability, control and status words at successive four-byte steps. Capability reports its association count in a low nibble. Control mirrors link control with enable, three aggregation selectors, checksum enable, config-request enable, partial-encryption mode, cipher selector, traffic class and high-byte identifier, plus distinct default-stream and TEE-limited markers and a stated identifier ceiling of 255. Status reports a low-nibble state with insecure encoded as zero and secure encoded as two, plus a top-bit failure latch.

Selective association resources use fixed offsets for requester identity filters and computed strides for address ranges. One identity word carries a middle-bits limit field, while a second identity word at a higher offset carries valid, base and segment subfields. Each address association spans twelve bytes with three computed words per index starting from a base near twenty; the first word packs valid plus low base and limit portions. Total selective extent grows linearly as a fixed header plus twelve bytes per association.

The CXL device extension numbered zero places capability and control bytes at low offsets. Capability advertises cache and memory aptitude in separate low bits and a managed-device count in a two-bit field. Control carries a memory-enable bit. At most two address ranges are described by per-index size and base register pairs spaced sixteen bytes apart; size words share valid, active, timeout and low-size subfields, while base words share a low-base subfield.

Further CXL extensions are numbered two through eight with gaps. Number two marks function mapping, three marks a port with a control word able to unmask reset propagation, four marks port shutdown handling with two phase controls each splitting timeout base and scale into low nibbles, five marks device shutdown handling, seven marks flexbus port status exposing cache and memory active bits, and eight marks register location with a descriptor word splitting bus index, block identity and low offset portions.

Process execution domain packs legacy behavior selectors into high bits above the low byte, covering uname versioning, address randomization, descriptor function pointers, zero-page mapping, layout compatibility, implied execute permission, address width limits, inode width, time granularity, timeout stickiness and a three-gigabyte limit. A defined subset clears on privilege change, covering implied execute, randomization, layout and zero-page mapping. Named personas combine a low-byte identity from zero through fifteen with selected behavior bits, and a low-byte mask isolates the identity.

Process descriptor creation reuses file-status encodings for nonblocking, thread-scoped, stale-clone and autokill behaviors. Signal targeting uses three low-bit selectors for thread, thread-group and process-group scope. Information queries use low-bit request flags distinguishing always-returned identity and credential fields from on-demand exit and dump fields plus a supported-mask query and dump detail selectors. Four published information sizes grow in eight-byte steps from sixty-four bytes, and dump outcome uses four low bits for crashed, skipped, user and privileged handling.

The process information carrier is a fixed-order record beginning with request-result and cgroup words, followed by process, group and parent identifiers, then eight credential identifiers for real, effective, saved and filesystem user and group, then a signed exit value, then a nested dump tuple of mask, signal, code and alignment pad, ending with a supported-feature word kept eight-byte aligned. Two self-reference aliases denote thread and thread-group scope.

Callers set desired extensions in the leading mask and the kernel ignores unknown bits, setting only bits for fields it actually populated and omitting bits whose data would not fit in the supplied size, so callers must recheck the returned mask before consuming fields. Identity and credential outputs may already be stale if the target exited during the call, but on success they were accurate for the intended process at handling time.

A descriptor filesystem exposes namespace retrieval and information query operations under a magic byte value of 255. Small operation numbers one through ten fetch distinct namespace handles for cgroup, IPC, mount, network, PID, child PID, time, child time, user and UTS, while operation eleven exchanges the information record bidirectionally.

Traffic control action payloads order attributes from kind and options through index, statistics, padding, cookie, flags, hardware statistics selectors, used statistics and in-hardware count, with a bounded cookie length of sixteen bytes and a maximum priority depth of thirty-two. Action behavior flags request no per-CPU statistics and skip hardware or software paths, while hardware reporting distinguishes immediate device queries from potentially delayed polled or asynchronous updates. Binding and replacement each use one for affirmative and zero for negative.

Packet verdicts form a signed sequence from minus one for unspecified through zero to eight, covering pass, reclassify, drop, pipeline, steal, queue, repeat, redirect and trap, with trap meaning surrender to CPU in hardware and drop-with-success in software. Numeric action families assign small integers to generic control, packet edit, mirror, address translation, extension matches, buffer edits, tagging, packet filter, connection mark, checksum, tunnel key, simple, interface and sampling roles, mirrored by a classifier identifier enumeration capped at 255, where policer aliases reuse the generic verdict encodings.

A policer record orders index, verdict, token limits, burst, MTU, average and peak rate descriptors, reference and bind counts and capability flags. A timing record orders install, last-use, expiry and first-use stamps as wide time values, while a counter record pairs reference and bind counts and a shared generator header orders index, capability, verdict and the two counts. Policer attributes progress from token bucket and rate descriptors through result, timing and wide rate extensions, with the maximum defined as one less than the sentinel.

Extended verdicts shift a local opcode into the top nibble starting at bit twenty-eight, masking the low twenty-eight bits as value and comparing after clearing those bits, with defined opcodes for jump and chain goto and the latter as maximum. Classifier offload flags independently request skipping hardware or software, report presence or absence in hardware, and enable verbose logging.
Each userspace header in this lane protects itself with a single inclusion guard macro so repeated inclusion yields one definition set.

Link and selective streams each expose a low-nibble state field; selective defines encodings for insecure and secure with failure signaled separately by a high-bit latch, while link likewise pairs its state nibble with a high-bit failure latch. Transition triggers and full state graphs are not visible in these fragments.

Consumers must treat link and selective failure latches, potentially delayed hardware statistics and possibly stale process identity outputs as advisory rather than synchronous truth, rechecking masks and status after operations that may race with peer failure messages, driver polling delays or target exit.

These headers export stable userspace contracts for PCI capability parsing, execution-domain selection, process-descriptor management and traffic-control configuration, intended for direct inclusion by user programs and for ioctl and netlink exchanges.
